🎙
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s
remarks
at the 8th meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan
(Moscow, October 5, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
It is a pleasure to open
the latest meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan
.
This dialogue mechanism of high standing has been in operation since 2016 meaning that this particular meeting marks
its 10th anniversary
and brings together countries that have a stake in establishing and maintaining equal and mutually beneficial partnership with the Afghan people. It offers an opportunity to hold
a substantive discussion of matters related to providing international assistance to Afghanistan
and, importantly, to do so in conjunction with Kabul.
☝️
August 2026 marked the fifth anniversary of Afghanistan’s liberation from
two decades of Western occupation
. The vast military machine of the US and its NATO allies crumbled in the face of the Afghan people’s fighting spirit and determination, forcing the occupiers to flee. A national government led by the Taliban movement came to power and established control over the country. I
t must be acknowledged that it has governed with a fair degree of success.
Afghan security forces are waging an uncompromising fight against ISIS and other terrorist groups
. Hundreds of militants have been eliminated, and a number of high-profile terrorist attacks, including those targeting foreign nationals and diplomatic missions, have been foiled. Importantly, helping strengthen Kabul’s counterterrorism capabilities by providing material and expert assistance and maintaining contacts between intelligence and law enforcement agencies
meets the interests of all of us
.
The measures the Afghan government is taking to combat illicit drug trafficking produce results
. According to expert assessments by
the UN Office on Drugs and Crime
, opiate production in that country
has declined by 90%
since 2022.
The Afghan economy continues to grow despite the tough sanctions imposed by Western countries
, which, under the pretext of protecting human rights, have cut the Islamic Emirate off from the international financial system and seized its national banking assets. This is what the West is practicing on a regular basis.
Unfortunately, the humanitarian situation in the country remains difficult
.
According to the UN
,
more than 17 million Afghans
- nearly half the population -
will face food shortages this coming winter
, and the total number of people in need of humanitarian aid will reach
22 million
. Clearly, relevant international agencies need to step up, and bilateral efforts need to be deployed to address the situation at hand.
Russia will continue to provide regular humanitarian aid
, and
another batch
will arrive in Afghanistan in the coming months.
❗️
The deployment of NATO military infrastructure in Afghanistan and neighbouring countries under any pretext whatsoever is categorically unacceptable
. As we know from history, presence of this kind carries the risk of destabilisation and heightened tensions and conflict. We have seen no other outcome from this kind of presence over the past several decades.
I am confident that your meeting will be
constructive
and contribute to
Afghanistan’s further development as an independent and sustainable state
, and help promote peace and stability throughout the region.

item.title: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov during talks with Foreign Minister of Afghanistan Amir Khan Muttaqi

Opening remarks
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov during talks with Foreign Minister of Afghanistan Amir Khan Muttaqi
(Moscow, October 5, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
I would like to emphasise that
we greatly value Kabul’s direct participation
in
the Moscow Format consultations on Afghanistan
.
We consider
this platform
the most effective forum for addressing the problems facing Afghanistan and the surrounding region
, not simply because it bears Moscow’s name, but because of the concrete results it delivers.
I would like to congratulate you on
the fifth anniversary of Afghanistan’s liberation from the NATO military presence
.
Five years is a short time to overcome
the consequences
of decades of occupation, but
your Government’s achievements are evident
, and we welcome them.
Achievements in combatting terrorism and drug trafficking are evident as well
. Your country has seen
170 new enterprises
open. In monetary terms,
exports have doubled
over the past five years. We are certainly encouraged by the start of construction of

item.title: ⚡️ Prosecutor General’s Office of the Russian Federation Following an application by the Prosecutor General’s Office of the Russian Federation,
item.description: ⚡️ Prosecutor General’s Office of the Russian Federation : Following an application by the Prosecutor General’s Office of the Russian Federation, Baltic nationalists have been recognised by a court as accomplices of Nazi Germany in war crimes and crimes against humanity committed against the Soviet people during the Great Patriotic War – a finding of legal significance. Recognition of this fact is not only an evident conclusion stemming from the principal legal findings of the Nuremberg Trials , but also a historical duty that society and the state owe to those who fought in the war, its veterans and its victims . ⚖️ It has been established that the Nazi invaders committed atrocities with the direct involvement of their accomplices – Latvian, Lithuanian and Estonian nationalists ( 13 individuals and five organisations ). According to records from the archives of Russia’s Federal Security Service , Foreign Ministry and Defence Ministry , as well as the State Archive of the Russian Federation , following Germany’s attack on the USSR , the Nazis recruited Baltic nationalists from among local residents to do their “dirty work” in the occupied territories . They carried out punitive operations against civilians and Soviet POWs. Through their actions, the territories of the Baltic countries – Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia – became killing grounds during the Great Patriotic War for POWs, Soviet officials and their families, and people suspected of sympathising with the Red Army. ▪️

⚡️
Prosecutor General’s Office of the Russian Federation
:
Following an application by the Prosecutor General’s Office of the Russian Federation,
Baltic nationalists
have been recognised by a court
as accomplices of Nazi Germany in war crimes and crimes against humanity committed against the Soviet people during the Great Patriotic War
– a finding of legal significance.
Recognition of this fact is not only
an evident conclusion
stemming from
the principal legal findings of the Nuremberg Trials
, but also
a historical duty
that society and the state owe to those who fought in the war, its veterans and
its victims
.
⚖️
It has been established that the Nazi invaders committed atrocities with the direct involvement of their accomplices –
Latvian, Lithuanian and Estonian nationalists
(
13 individuals and five organisations
).
According to records from the archives of
Russia’s Federal Security Service
,
Foreign Ministry
and
Defence Ministry
, as well as
the State Archive of the Russian Federation
, following
Germany’s attack on the USSR
,
the Nazis recruited Baltic nationalists from among local residents to do their “dirty work” in the occupied territories
. They carried out
punitive operations
against civilians and Soviet POWs.
Through their actions, the territories of the Baltic countries –
Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia
– became killing grounds during the Great Patriotic War for POWs, Soviet officials and their families, and people suspected of sympathising with the Red Army.
▪️
In total, Baltic collaborators killed more than 1.5 million people during the war and the post-war years.
***
Since the early 1990s, the authorities of today’s Baltic countries have pursued
a deliberate state policy of distorting the USSR’s role in the Great Patriotic War and
its Victory over Nazism
. Collaborators associated with Nazi criminals, along with their organisations, are being
glorified
.
This
contradicts
the Verdict of the Nuremberg Tribunal
regarding responsibility for
the Second World War, its causes and its outcomes
, as well as the provisions of the UN General Assembly resolution
“Combating glorification of Nazism, neo-Nazism and other practices that contribute to fuelling contemporary forms of racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance”
.
In effect, it serves to justify Nazi crimes.
❗️
Countering these destructive trends is fundamental to preserving historical memory, preventing the falsification of history and protecting the national interests of the Russian Federation.

item.title: 🇷🇺 #Announcement On October 4-6, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste
item.description: #Announcement 🇷🇺 🇹🇱 On October 4-6, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste Bendito Freitas will pay an official visit to Moscow. On October 6, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov will hold talks with Bendito Freitas . The Ministers will exchange views on a wide range of issues on the bilateral agenda , including deepening political dialogue, developing cooperation in trade, the economy and humanitarian sphere, and improving the legal framework governing relations between the two countries. They are also expected to discuss key international and regional issues . #RussiaTimorLeste

item.title: ⚡️ #KievRegimeCrimes Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
item.description: #KievRegimeCrimes ⚡️ Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Rodion Miroshnik : PHOTO FACTS & EVIDENCE of crimes committed by Ukrainian armed forces over the week of September 28 – October 4, 2026 : ▪️ September 28 – balloons carrying propaganda leaflets, a radio repeater and Lepestok anti-personnel mines were shot down over the Belgorod Region. ▪️ September 28 – a UAV strike on an apartment building in Voronezh, Voronezh Region. The overnight UAV raid on the city’s residential neighbourhoods resulted in injuries to 13 civilians. ▪️ September 30 – a UAV strike on a grocery store in Novaya Kakhovka, Kherson Region. ▪️ September 30 – a UAV strike on a civilian car in the village of Raiskoye, Kherson Region. ▪️ October 2 – a UAV strike on an EMERCOM vehicle in Donetsk, DPR. Eight rescue workers were injured. ▪️ October 2 – a UAV strike on an apartment building in Donetsk, DPR. A 76-year-old civilian was injured. ▪️ October 3 – the aftermath of a massive UAV raid on residential neighbourhoods in Belgorod, Belgorod Region. Two civilians were killed and 12 were injured. ▪️ October 3 – a UAV strike on a civilian car in Belgorod, Belgorod Region. ▪️ October 3 – a UAV strike on a private home in Donetsk, DPR. A civilian was injured. ▪️ October 3 – a UAV strike on a civilian car in the village of Kazinka, Belgorod Region.
